criteria:
The Signal reads every filing whose header prints "Filing Type: Annual Report" and "Status: Member". It reads no index code: which reports are annual is what each report says of itself. A filing whose header the register has not read, which includes every report filed on paper, is not among the reports it evaluates, and neither is any other kind of report or a report filed as a candidate.

For each report it reads, it evaluates the report only where each of these holds, and otherwise records the first reason that fails. The header prints a filing year. The filing year is 2025: the instructions the register has read are those for calendar year 2025, and a later year is a new version, read against its own instructions. It is the earliest annual report the index lists for this officeholder and filing year, by the date the index gives it and then by its identifier: a later one is not evaluated, because firing on a second copy of a report compared on time would be false about the report. The date the Clerk's index gives the report, the Filing Date the report prints and the date its signature line gives can all be read, and are the same day. The roster records a swearing-in for the officeholder. The officeholder served more than 60 days of the filing year, counted from the later of 1 January and the swearing-in the roster records to 31 December.

The original due date is 15 May of the year after the filing year, or the first business day after it where 15 May is a Saturday, a Sunday or a federal holiday. The latest date is 90 days after 15 May or 90 days after the original due date, whichever is later, and the first business day after that where it falls on a Saturday, a Sunday or a holiday. The Committee's Guide does not move the end of a 90-day extension for a weekend; the Signal takes the later day wherever the rules could be read two ways, so that it never fires on a report that any reading of them would leave within an extension. No extension the statute allows outside a combat zone reaches past the latest date. For filing year 2025 neither date moves: the original due date is Friday 15 May 2026 and the latest date Thursday 13 August 2026.

A report dated on or before its original due date is evaluated, and the Signal does not fire. A report dated after its original due date and on or before the latest date is not evaluated: an extension may cover it, and the register does not decide whether one does. A report dated the day after the latest date is not evaluated either, because the register has not established in which time zone the filing system prints the date, and a report submitted late in the evening could carry the next day's. The Signal fires for a report dated two days or more after the latest date. The Finding names the report and the officeholder the register attributes it to, and gives the report's date, the original due date, the latest date, and the days after the latest date. No extension notice, attributed or set aside, enters the Signal. Beside the result, each officeholder's page lists every row the index gives at the seat under the officeholder's surname with the code the Committee's extension forms carry, attributed or set aside, with what its header prints where the register could read it; the list decides nothing.

    original due = 15 May (Y + 1), moved to the next business day
    latest       = max(15 May (Y + 1) + 90, original due + 90), moved to the next business day
    fires        where report date >= latest + 2, for Y = 2025

The implementation that writes the Findings is [`src/signals/annual-report-after-extension-limit.py`](../../src/signals/annual-report-after-extension-limit.py). The reference implementation, [`src/signals/annual-report-after-extension-limit.ts`](../../src/signals/annual-report-after-extension-limit.ts), shares no code with it and must agree with it on every known-answer case and every row of the register; `python tools/rebuild.py <finding-id>` regenerates any Finding from the rows it names. Each carries its own copy of the federal calendar, and the known answers hold that calendar for later filing years too. This file, both implementations and the known-answer cases are frozen with the version: the Signal's row carries the SHA-256 of each, and a change to any of them is a new version.
description: A Member of the U.S. House of Representatives, a Delegate or the Resident Commissioner who serves more than 60 days in a calendar year is required to file an annual financial disclosure report for it by 15 May of the next year, its original due date, and outside a combat zone extensions may add at most 90 days in total. This Signal compares the date on each such annual report for filing year 2025 with the latest date any extension the statute allows outside a combat zone could reach, and reports a result only where the report's date is later, stating by how many days. Before that date it does not decide whether an extension covers a report: it says the report is within the time an extension may cover, and does not evaluate it.
name: Annual financial disclosure report dated after the latest date an extension could reach
not_saying:
This Signal does not say the House Committee on Ethics found a report late, assessed a fee or waived one: Oath reads none of the Committee's decisions, which is not to say none exist. This Signal does not say whether an extension was granted for a report, or covers it: it reads no extension notice. This Signal does not see a report whose header the register cannot read, such as one filed on paper, or a report the index sets aside under a sitting member's surname because the given names differ or the index prints another seat, which waits for the maintainer to decide by hand, so a member whose report is among those cannot be among those on which it fires. This Signal does not see an extension for service in a combat zone, which the statute allows beyond 90 days; every Finding says so.

This Signal reads only a report's date, not what the report lists, and not why the report carries the date it does. It does not reach a member sworn in with 60 days or fewer of the filing year left, for whom the rule asks no annual report for that year; a member who left before the roster the register read; a candidate for the seat; a filing year other than 2025; or a Congress's second year, whose reports are due after the Congress's terms end, when the register attributes no row of it by name. Where the index lists no annual report the register attributes to a member, this Signal says nothing, and the page says exactly that, never that a report was not filed. The Signal relies on the date the Clerk's index gives a report, and reads it only where the report's own Filing Date and signature date agree with it; where all three are wrong together, a Finding repeats the error, and the correction follows the record by supersession, never by removal. It does not rank, total or compare officeholders.

standard.citation: 5 U.S.C. § 13103(d), (g)(1), of the Ethics in Government Act of 1978 (5 U.S.C. chapter 131)

worked_example.expected: Against [`fixtures/annual-report-after-extension-limit/cases.json`](../../fixtures/annual-report-after-extension-limit/cases.json), seventeen cases with no person in them, each answer worked by hand and by a separate script, and a calendar for six filing years. For calendar year 2025, 15 May 2026 is a Friday, so the original due date is that day, and the latest date is Thursday 13 August 2026. A report dated 13 August is within the time an extension may cover and is not evaluated; one dated 14 August is the day after, and is not evaluated; one dated 15 August fires, with this text: "This is an annual financial disclosure report for calendar year 2025. The Clerk's index dates it 2026-08-15, the same date the report prints as its filing date and its signature line gives. Its original due date was 2026-05-15. Outside a combat zone the statute lets extensions add at most 90 days to it (5 U.S.C. § 13103(d), (g)(1)), so the latest date any such extension could reach was 2026-08-13. The report is dated 2 days after that latest date. The register cannot see an extension for service in a combat zone, which 5 U.S.C. § 13103(g)(2) allows beyond 90 days." A second annual report for the same filing year, dated after an earlier one, is not evaluated. A report whose printed Filing Date differs from its index date is not evaluated, whatever its dates. A report for filing year 2026 is not evaluated: for it, 15 May 2027 is a Saturday, so the calendar would move the original due date to Monday 17 May and the latest date to Monday 16 August, and the known answers hold that arithmetic for the version that reads that year's instructions. A report whose header says "Amendment Report", or "Status: Congressional Candidate", or a paper report with no header the register can read, is not among the reports the Signal evaluates.

criteria:
The Signal reads every report of form type `House-PTR` in the register. A report the register did not read, which is a scanned paper filing, is not evaluated: its transaction dates are printed in the document, and the register reads no scanned document. A report whose date in the Clerk's index cannot be read is not evaluated.

For every other report it takes each transaction row in turn and evaluates it only where the rule plainly reaches it. Otherwise it counts the row, with the first of these reasons that applies. The report marks the row with a filing status other than New, or with none: an amendment is filed after the report it amends, and the rule measures the original. Its transaction date is not a real calendar date written as the report writes dates. Its asset is not coded `ST`, `CS`, `OP` or `CT`, or carries no code. The Clerk's legend defines the codes, and the register has not read it at its source; the rows the reports code so name stocks, corporate bonds and notes, options and cryptocurrencies, which the Committee's form covers as stocks, bonds and other securities, cryptocurrencies among them. Every other code is counted and not evaluated: the Committee's instructions keep widely held funds, real property and some other assets off these reports, though some reports list them, and the register has not read the instructions to settle where others belong, government securities among them. It is coded `ST` and its printed name calls it an ETF, a widely held fund. Its amount is $1,000 or less, which the rule does not reach. The roster records no swearing-in date for the officeholder, or the transaction is dated before the swearing-in the roster records for this Congress: the roster records that date, not the start of a person's service, and a returning Member's earlier transactions were under the same rule, but the register holds no earlier index against which to tell a transaction first reported now from one reported before, so this version does not evaluate them. The transaction is dated after the report. Its deadline, below, falls before 2025: the instructions the register has read are the CY 2025 form's, and earlier instructions have not always said the same thing about a weekend.

For a row it evaluates, the deadline is the earlier of 30 days after the notification date the report prints and 45 days after the transaction date. Where the report prints no notification date, or one that cannot be read, or one before the transaction date or after the report's own date, the 30-day limit is not applied and the deadline is 45 days after the transaction, which does not depend on it. Days are calendar days: 30 days after 13 January is 12 February. The deadline does not move when it falls on a weekend or a federal holiday, as the Committee's instructions state. Where the two limits fall on the same day, the 45-day limit is named as setting it.

A row is after the deadline when the Clerk's index dates the report later than the deadline, by the difference in days. The Signal fires for a report when at least one row it evaluated is after the deadline. The Finding names the report and the officeholder the register attributes it to. For every row after the deadline it gives the dates as printed, the deadline, the limit that set it and the days after; whether the report prints a notification date later than 45 days after the transaction, and how many days after that notification the index dates the report; and, where the deadline fell on a Saturday, a Sunday or a federal holiday as 5 U.S.C. § 6103 lists them on the days observed, the first business day after it. The sentence says so where that decides the Finding, which is where the index dates the report on or before that first business day. The Finding also counts the rows on the report the Signal evaluated and the rows it did not, by reason, and carries the frame.

    in scope(row) = marked New; coded ST, CS, OP or CT, and not an ST named as an ETF;
                    over $1,000; traded on or after this Congress's swearing-in and on or
                    before the report
    deadline(row) = min(notified + 30, traded + 45)   when traded <= notified <= report date
                  = traded + 45                       otherwise
    after(row)    = report date - deadline(row)       after when 1 or more, for a deadline
                                                      in 2025 or later

The implementation that writes the Findings is [`src/signals/stock-act-ptr-after-deadline.py`](../../src/signals/stock-act-ptr-after-deadline.py). The reference implementation, [`src/signals/stock-act-ptr-after-deadline.ts`](../../src/signals/stock-act-ptr-after-deadline.ts), shares no code with it and must agree with it on every known-answer case and every row of the register; `python tools/rebuild.py <finding-id>` regenerates any Finding from the rows it names. This file, both implementations and the known-answer cases are frozen with the version: the Signal's row carries the SHA-256 of each, and a change to any of them is a new version.
description: A Member of the House reports a purchase, sale or exchange of stocks, bonds, commodity futures or other securities over $1,000 on a Periodic Transaction Report, due within 30 days of being notified of the transaction and in no case later than 45 days after it. This Signal sets the date the Clerk's public index gives each House report the register has read beside the dates the report prints for each transaction on it that the rule plainly reaches. It fires for a report when, for at least one of those transactions, the index date is later than the deadline, and it records by how many days and for which transactions.
name: Periodic Transaction Report dated after the STOCK Act deadline
not_saying:
It does not say the House Committee on Ethics found a report late, assessed a fee, waived one, or took any other action: the register sees none of the Committee's decisions. Under the Committee's instructions a fee applies to a report filed more than 30 days late, and the Committee may waive it; the register computes no fee for anyone. It does not say the officeholder meant to delay a report, knew of a transaction earlier than the report says, or gained anything from its timing. It says nothing about the transactions themselves, which the rule requires reported and does not prohibit, and nothing about who holds an asset: many rows are a spouse's, a dependent child's or held jointly, whether or not the filer marked them, and a row the filer lists under a trust, a foundation or another account is evaluated as listed.

A report may list transactions the rule does not require on it, and this Signal does not evaluate them. Nor does it evaluate reports the register has not read, rows marked Amended or Deleted or marked with no status, or transactions dated before this Congress's swearing-in, so a page on which it did not fire may still hold such a report or row, and the page says how many; an officeholder whose reports are all scanned paper cannot be among those on which it fired, whatever the reports show. A transaction reported on more than one report is evaluated on each. The Signal relies on the date the Clerk's public index gives a report and on the dates the report prints. The register has not compared the index date with the date signed on each report, or learned in which time zone the index keeps it; where a Finding turns on a day or two, its table shows how many. Where either date is wrong, a Finding repeats the error, and the correction follows the record by supersession, never by removal. It does not rank, total or compare officeholders, and a report with many rows after the deadline is one report.

standard.citation: 5 U.S.C. § 13105(l), added by the STOCK Act of 2012 (Pub. L. 112-105)

worked_example.expected: Against [`fixtures/stock-act-ptr-after-deadline/cases.json`](../../fixtures/stock-act-ptr-after-deadline/cases.json), thirty-six cases with no person in them, each answer worked by hand. A transaction on 2 January 2025, notified on 20 January, has a deadline of 16 February, 45 days after the transaction and earlier than 30 days after the notification: a report dated 16 February is on time and one dated 17 February is after the deadline by 1 day. A report dated 10 April 2025 listing a transaction of 3 March notified the same day (deadline 2 April), one of 20 March notified the same day (deadline 19 April) and one marked Amended fires for the first row only, with this text: "The Clerk's index dates this report 2025-04-10, which is later than the deadline the rule sets for 1 of the 2 transactions on it that this Signal evaluated, by 8 days. The deadline is the earlier of 30 days after the notification date the report prints and 45 days after the transaction date (5 U.S.C. § 13105(l))." A transaction of 31 July 2025 notified the same day has a deadline of Saturday 30 August; Monday 1 September was Labor Day, so a report dated Tuesday 2 September is after the deadline by 3 days, and its sentence ends: "For that transaction the deadline fell on a Saturday, and the Clerk's index dates the report on or before the first business day after it, 2025-09-02 (Labor Day, 2025-09-01, was a federal holiday); the Committee's instructions for these reports state that a due date on a weekend or holiday does not move." A notification date printed before the transaction date is not applied, so a report of 5 May for a transaction of 10 April with a printed notification of 1 April does not fire, where applying that date would have put it 4 days after 1 May. A row coded `GS` is counted and not evaluated, whatever its dates.
